## [dead-code] qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:321 Redundant memset(sp, 0, sizeof(*sp)) at the top of drain_state_into
VERDICT: CONFIRMED

DETAIL: drain_state_into zeroes the caller's output struct at line 321, then builds the entire state in a zero-initialized local (line 322: struct hybrid_state_v1 s = {0}) and unconditionally copies it out at line 473 (*sp = s) - the only paths that skip line 473 call exit(2) (lines 432, 495-499 are in callees that terminate the process), and the sole caller drain_state_to_file (line 508) reads the struct only after the call returns. hybrid_state_v1 is padding-free by design (include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h asserts every field offset), so the {0} local plus struct assignment already determines every output byte; the memset writes bytes that are always overwritten.

SAFETY: The memset's effect is fully shadowed by the unconditional *sp = s on every returning path; removing it cannot change any byte of the written state file.

VERIFY_WITH: tests/plugin/test_plugin_drain_exit_code.sh plus a hybrid e2e with --verify (scripts/run_e2e.sh FILTER=rt_csr), which byte-compares the drained state.

VERIFIER_NOTES: Verified all four legs of the claim. (1) drain_state_into is static with exactly one caller (hybrid_handoff.c:508); grep across andesim, andesim-demo, and vsim_andesim finds no other source reference. (2) The function body has no return/goto and the plugin has no setjmp/longjmp; the only path skipping the unconditional '*sp = s' at line 473 is exit(2) at line 432, which kills the process before the caller could read the struct. (3) hybrid_state_v1 is provably padding-free: the sum of all member sizes (7504 bytes) equals the sizeof locked by state_abi_check.h:106, and every field offset is asserted - so 's = {0}' plus the explicit assignments determine every byte, and the struct assignment copies every byte (the C padding-bytes-unspecified caveat has nothing to apply to). (4) The caller reads the struct only after the call returns, writing exactly sizeof bytes to the file. The memset at line 321 is therefore fully shadowed on every observable path; removing it cannot change the state file bytes, sidecars, log output, or exit codes.

## [dead-code] qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:559 Unreachable kind guard in on_handoff_boundary; marker mode registers permanently no-op exec callbacks on EXIT markers
VERDICT: CONFIRMED

DETAIL: on_handoff_boundary (line 556) is registered only in pc_mode (line 632), and its HandoffSite is always created with kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER (line 629), so the guard at line 559 can never fire. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# PC-trigger contract: the drained resume PC equals the --pc-start boundary.
#
# The drain callback fires BEFORE the trigger insn executes, so the captured
# state is pre-execution. A marker is an architectural NOP and may be skipped
# (resume at vaddr+size), but a pc boundary is real user code: if the plugin
# reports vaddr+size, the boundary insn executes on NEITHER leg (e.g. a
# skipped vsetivli leaves vtype.vill set and the vsim window faults on the
# first vector op). The plugin must report the boundary's own vaddr so the
# insn runs inside the measured window.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF     any fixture with a `main` symbol (default: vplat_hello.elf)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-vplat_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
command -v "${NM:-nm}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NM=nm
ENTER_HEX=$("$NM" "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$3 == "main" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$ENTER_HEX" ] || { echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: no main in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
ENTER=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$ENTER_HEX")

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-pcresume-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=$ENTER" \
  </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$ENTER)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: resume PC != pc-start boundary $ENTER:"
  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
echo "[pc_trigger_resume_pc] PASS: drain resumes at the boundary insn ($ENTER)"

# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make            # build both
#   make clean
#
# Output (in this directory):
#   libhybrid_handoff.so    -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotIterationLoop.so  -- hot inner-loop detector (`andesim profile`)

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

.PHONY: all clean

all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so

libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)

# hotIterationLoop is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not
# HYBRID_INCLUDE.
libhotIterationLoop.so: hotIterationLoop.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotIterationLoop.c $(LIBS)

clean:
	rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so
